solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Yes-man shielding unknown officer with blunt refusal (9)

indicatorNotes.shielding: to shield something is to put yourself round it, so the refusal wraps round the other letters

blocks.note: algebra's unknowns are x, y and z

annotation.surface: A fawning subordinate covers for a colleague while someone else gets a flat no.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in the refusal is dropped, as crossword grids always do. The wrapper splits after its very first letter, which makes the join hard to see.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the flatterer who agrees with everything a superior says is both a sycophant and a yes-man.

entries.clue: Ornamental plant is the kind you trim, collecting the ends (5)

indicatorNotes.collecting the ends: the ends of words are their final letters, and collecting them strings those letters together

blocks.note: the final letter of each of the five words

annotation.surface: A gardener says this decorative plant is the sort you prune, gathering up the clippings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trim' and 'ends' both look like gardening; together they only tell you to read the last letter of each word.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: sedum, or stonecrop, is a fleshy-leaved succulent grown in rockeries and borders for its starry flowers.

entries.clue: Pundits yapping about bespectacled party organizer holding key (10,7)

indicatorNotes.holding: to hold something is to have it inside your grasp, so the bespectacled phrase keeps the key within it

blocks.note: the Mad Hatter hosts the tea party in Alice in Wonderland

annotation.surface: Talking heads chatter about a party host in spectacles who has the key.
annotation.walkthrough: The key goes in straight after the G of the glasses. Chattering classes is a British phrase for the educated people who air opinions on current affairs.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase mocks commentators and opinion-formers who talk endlessly, which is exactly pundits yapping.

entries.clue: Finish off small person, a hero in play (9)

indicatorNotes.Finish off: to finish something off is to take away its finish, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: PYGMY with its last letter gone
a lion is a brave person, a hero

annotation.surface: An order to kill off a little man so a hero can triumph on stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finish off' reads as murder but only trims a letter. Shaw's play about Eliza Doolittle later became the musical My Fair Lady.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the answer is George Bernard Shaw's 1913 comedy, one play among many.

entries.clue: First of subs in front of aircraft carrier that’s off course (6)

indicatorNotes.First of: the first of a word is its opening letter
indicatorNotes.in: the letter is placed in the string that follows it
indicatorNotes.front of: the front of a word is its opening letter

annotation.surface: A submarine leads an aircraft carrier that has wandered off its route.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Aircraft carrier' is not one thing: 'front of aircraft' and 'carrier' are separate pieces, and the S slips in between them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something that has strayed from its proper route has gone off course.

entries.clue: Record piece of law that’s useful when preparing suit (4,7)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes what the answer is for rather than naming it
annotation.surface: A lawyer's document that comes in handy when getting a lawsuit ready.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Law' and 'suit' paint a courtroom; the suit is one a tailor makes.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: tailors take a customer's measurements with one before cutting the cloth for a suit.

entries.clue: Strangely reformed, having eliminated one right or liberty (7)

indicatorNotes.Strangely: something done strangely is done in an odd way, so the letters come out in an odd order
indicatorNotes.having eliminated: to eliminate is to get rid of, so the named letter is taken out of the word

annotation.surface: Someone oddly reformed has given up a single right, or their liberty.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder has two Rs; only one goes, and the seven letters left rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the state of being free to act, speak or move as you choose goes by either word.

entries.clue: Pay people running event (4,4)

blocks.note: to foot the bill = to pay
a race = a people, a nation

annotation.surface: Someone must pay the staff who run an event.
annotation.walkthrough: 'People running event' looks like event organisers; the last two words are the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: a contest decided by who runs fastest, as opposed to one on horseback or wheels.

entries.clue: Mistake of singer beset by expressions of doubt (7)

indicatorNotes.beset by: to be beset is to be surrounded on all sides, so the singer sits between the two hesitations

blocks.note: one who sings to the police is an informer, a rat

annotation.surface: A vocalist fluffs a line and is surrounded by hesitant ums and ers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Singer' is the informer who sings, not a vocalist. 'Expressions of doubt' is plural because it supplies both halves of the wrapping.
annotation.definitionFit: A Latin borrowing: the word means an error, especially a printing mistake listed in a correction slip.

entries.clue: Board’s conclusion is having significant role in reducing charges (11)

indicatorNotes.conclusion: the conclusion of a word is where it ends, its last letter

annotation.surface: A board has concluded it will play a big part in cutting fees.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a company board's decision; 'Board' only lends its final letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in commerce: knocking money off the price asked is cutting the charge.

entries.clue: He’s in team at sea that controls sail (9)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a relative clause describing the answer

indicatorNotes.at sea: to be at sea is to be confused, so the letters are in a muddle

annotation.surface: A crew member at sea whose job is handling the sail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At sea' sounds nautical, which suits the answer, but here it means muddled.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: on a sailing boat this rope sets the angle of the mainsail to the wind.

entries.clue: Damage following cold spell (5)

indicatorNotes.following: what follows comes after, so the damage is placed after the cold

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: Damage done after a period of cold weather.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cold spell' is a weather phrase; split it, and 'spell' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in magic: an incantation that bewitches is both a spell and a charm.

entries.clue: Window on left part of church (7)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue one thing on another sits above it, so the window comes first

annotation.surface: A window on the left-hand side of a church.
annotation.walkthrough: Churches are full of windows, but this window is an opportunity.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the chancel is the area round the altar at the east end, reserved for clergy and choir.

entries.clue: It appears to be missed by other players in a team (5)

annotation.definition: It appears to be missed by other players

blocks.note: a team, as in picking sides

annotation.surface: Something in a sports team that the other players seem to miss.
annotation.walkthrough: The players are actors, not sportsmen; the team is the only sporting part.
annotation.definitionFit: A theatre convention: a remark spoken to the audience is supposed to go unheard by the rest of the cast on stage.

entries.clue: It’s the interest taken in it that makes his job rewarding (11)

annotation.definition: It’s the interest taken in it that makes his job rewarding

blocks.clueFragment: It’s the interest taken in it
blocks.note: reads as enthusiasm for the work; means the percentage charged on a loan

annotation.surface: Someone who finds their work fulfilling because they care about it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Interest' reads as enthusiasm and 'rewarding' as satisfying; both are money words here.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the person whose income is the interest charged on loans literally profits from the interest taken.

entries.clue: Some beer for man on board (7)

blocks.note: beer drawn from the cask or keg, or a single swallow of it
a counter in the board game Americans call checkers

annotation.surface: A pint is ordered for a sailor aboard ship.
annotation.walkthrough: The board is a games board, not a ship's deck; draughts is the British name for checkers.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: beer on tap is draught beer, and each counter in the game of draughts is a draught, a man in the game's jargon.

entries.clue: Proverbial thief taking equivalent of money? That’s off-putting (15)

annotation.definition: Proverbial thief taking equivalent of money

blocks.clueFragment: Proverbial thief taking equivalent of money
blocks.note: the proverb's thief of time, and time is money
read literally: the act of putting things off

annotation.surface: A famous thief makes off with the equivalent of cash, which is off-putting.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half chains two sayings, the thief proverb and 'time is money'. 'Off-putting' is not unpleasant but putting-off.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the proverb names delay as the thief of time, and delaying is the habit of putting things off.

entries.clue: Group liking each other in social media — it may turn out badly (6,10,7)

indicatorNotes.badly: letters that turn out badly go wrong, ending up in the wrong order

blocks.clueFragment: social media — it may turn out

anagram.fodder: SOCIAL MEDIA IT MAY TURN OUT

annotation.surface: A warning that a clique of online friends may end in tears.
annotation.walkthrough: All 23 letters from 'social media' to 'out' are fodder; 'turn' looks like the instruction but is part of it.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase describes a group whose members keep praising one another, a gently mocking name for a clique.

entries.clue: High-flier, possibly, producing superior performance on course (6)

blocks.note: a small bird, which may fly high
in golf, a hole completed one stroke under par

annotation.surface: A top achiever turns in a fine display on a training course.
annotation.walkthrough: The course is a golf course, and 'possibly' flags that a high-flier here is a bird rather than a successful person.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a child's word for a little bird, and golf's score of one under par, better than the expected score.

entries.clue: Saint leaves much to be desired in cooking (5)

annotation.definition2: leaves much to be desired in cooking

blocks.note: a fourth-century bishop of Caesarea, one of the Cappadocian Fathers

blocks.clueFragment: leaves much to be desired in cooking
blocks.note: a herb whose leaves cooks want

annotation.surface: A holy man is a disappointing cook.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaves much to be desired' is an idiom for poor; here the leaves are herb leaves that cooks desire.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the name of the Cappadocian saint, and the aromatic herb prized in Italian cooking.

entries.clue: My demand for attention met by new guards (8)

indicatorNotes.met by: one thing met by another is joined by it, so the letter comes up against the end of the phrase

annotation.surface: Someone insists on being noticed and the new security staff are the audience.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My demand for attention' is read as the words spoken aloud, not described.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: men posted to keep watch over a building at night are guards.

entries.clue: Outshine East European, securing film parts (7)

indicatorNotes.securing: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the two letters hold the film parts between them

blocks.note: clips are short extracts of film

annotation.surface: An Eastern European actor steals the show by landing roles in movies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'East European' reads as one person; it is two separate letters that form the outside.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: as the moon blots out the sun, one person can overshadow another's brilliance.

entries.clue: Job permit son is twice changing for artist (4-13)

indicatorNotes.twice: twice means two times, so the word before it is used two times
indicatorNotes.changing: letters that are changing will not stay in the order given

annotation.surface: A work permit for a son keeps changing so that he can train as an artist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Job permit' reads as a work visa; the two words go to different places.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: painters such as Cezanne, Gauguin and Van Gogh, who followed Impressionism, belong to this school.

entries.clue: Person’s beginning alteration of my robe (6)

indicatorNotes.alteration of: to alter something is to change it, as a tailor alters a robe, so the letters change order

annotation.surface: Someone starts altering my dressing gown.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Person's beginning' reads as someone starting a job; it means where a person begins.
annotation.definitionFit: A biological sense: every human life starts as a developing organism in the womb.

entries.clue: Like best and worst, verbally (10)

blocks.note: reads as a pair of opposites
means taken as verbs, where both mean defeat

annotation.surface: A remark comparing extremes in speech.
annotation.walkthrough: Best and worst look like opposites, but as verbs both mean defeat: to best someone, to worst someone. 'Verbally' means as verbs.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: two words with the same meaning share this property, and these two do when used as verbs.

entries.clue: Model inside atrium scaled down (12)

indicatorNotes.Model: to model clay is to shape it, so the letters are reshaped

annotation.surface: A small-scale model placed inside a hallway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model' and 'scaled down' suggest a model railway, and 'Model' tempts as MINI; it is the verb that reshapes the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something made in a much smaller version has been reduced in scale.

entries.clue: Imprison one after another, as suggested by hearing (6)

indicatorNotes.as suggested by hearing: hearing is the sense of sound, so the word is chosen for how it is heard, not how it is spelt

annotation.surface: Locking prisoners up one at a time, as a court hearing proposed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' sounds legal, like the imprisonment; it asks you to listen.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to confine people, especially enemy nationals in wartime, without trial.

entries.clue: Part of tree containing small place for rest of birds (5)

indicatorNotes.containing: to contain is to hold within, so the part of the tree holds the small letter

blocks.note: a root is part of a tree
S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: Part of a tree where birds settle down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rest of' tempts as an instruction to drop a letter; the definition is a place where birds rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the perch or tree where birds settle for the night.

entries.clue: Roof of eating area a panel protects (6)

indicatorNotes.protects: to protect something is to shield it on all sides, so the panel wraps round the letter

blocks.note: a plate is a flat panel of metal or glass

annotation.surface: A board shelters the ceiling of a dining room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eating area' suggests a canteen; it is the mouth.
annotation.definitionFit: An anatomical description: the hard and soft palate form the upper surface of the mouth, the place we eat with.

entries.clue: Position of insect after temperature’s dropped (5)

indicatorNotes.’s dropped: 'has dropped': something dropped falls away, so the letter falls out of the word

blocks.note: T is the symbol for temperature in physics; it is removed

annotation.surface: Where an insect sits once the weather cools.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' orders the events in the surface; the letter is simply dropped from the end of the insect.
annotation.definitionFit: A Latin borrowing: the word means a place, the particular position where something happens.

entries.clue: Southern states collectively greeting Oriental food (5)

annotation.surface: The American South jointly welcomes Asian cuisine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Southern states' reads as the American South; it splits into two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish is one Eastern food.

entries.clue: Apart from openers, are we in fact together to perform again? (2-5)

indicatorNotes.Apart from openers: the openers of words are their first letters, and apart from them means without them
indicatorNotes.together: put together, so the four remnants join up

annotation.surface: Performers ask whether they are back together for a reunion show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Openers' are the opening letters, dropped from all four words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: to act out a past event or scene once more.

entries.clue: Boat’s propeller modified for liner — good (9)

indicatorNotes.modified: something modified has been changed, so the letters are changed round

annotation.surface: A ship's propeller has been adapted to fit an ocean liner, which is a good thing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Propeller' suggests a screw; this propeller is a person with an oar.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the Venetian boatman drives a gondola along with a single oar, so he is what propels it.

entries.clue: Detect water or steam? (6)

blocks.note: H2O in any form except the frozen one

annotation.surface: Trying to identify whether something is liquid or vapour.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a pun: split the answer 3-3 and water and steam are both forms of H2O that it describes.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for spotting something, and a split reading that describes any H2O that is not frozen.

entries.clue: Teachers’ leader was in charge of second class for change (9)

indicatorNotes.leader: the leader of a word is the letter at its head

blocks.note: in British schools a form is a class or year group

annotation.surface: A head of the teachers' union took charge of Year 2 to shake things up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Teachers' leader' looks like a union boss; only the first letter is wanted. The school sense of form is British.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to alter something thoroughly in form or character is to change it.

entries.clue: Quote three lines about one consumed with European dish from Italy (11)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the lines go round the eater
indicatorNotes.with: with means along with, so the last letter is added on

blocks.note: a tag is a stock quotation

annotation.surface: A menu entry quoting a few lines about someone eating an Italian meal.
annotation.walkthrough: The three Ls do not stay together: one goes before the eater and two after.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: long flat ribbons of egg pasta, a classic of Emilia-Romagna.

entries.clue: Unable to interpret odd Mongolian clue’s content (11)

indicatorNotes.odd: odd means strange, so the letters are in a strange order
indicatorNotes.content: the content of a word is what is inside it, its middle letters

annotation.surface: Someone cannot make sense of a strange Mongolian crossword hint.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Odd' might suggest odd letters, but here it rearranges. The 's in 'clue's' is possessive.
annotation.definitionFit: A description by consequence: someone who speaks only one language cannot translate between two.

entries.clue: Fruit and large quantity of cereal on board American vessel (7)

indicatorNotes.large quantity of: a large quantity is most of it, so the grain loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.on board: cargo on board sits inside a vessel, so the grain goes inside the pot

annotation.surface: Fruit and a big sack of grain loaded on to an American ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, which is why 'on board' reads naturally; it is a cooking pot.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the soft orange stone fruit is one of many fruits.

entries.clue: Be prepared to consider appearance (11)

blocks.note: the verb: to tolerate or allow
the noun: a face or its expression

annotation.surface: Advice to be ready to think about how things look.
annotation.walkthrough: The verb is usually negative: someone will not countenance an idea.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: as a verb it means to entertain or tolerate an idea, and as a noun it means someone's face or look.

entries.clue: Pasta split and reassembled as bar food (5)

indicatorNotes.split and reassembled: something split and reassembled is broken apart and put back differently, so the letters change order

annotation.surface: Pasta broken up and rearranged to serve as pub snacks.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a kitchen instruction; both fodder and answer are food.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: small Spanish savoury dishes, traditionally served with drinks in bars.

entries.clue: Something to play from India embraced by Harrison, for one (5)

indicatorNotes.embraced by: to be embraced is to be held in someone's arms, so the letter sits inside

blocks.note: I = India in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: An Indian instrument taken up by George Harrison.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is true: the Beatle George Harrison famously played the Indian instrument.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the long-necked lute of Indian classical music is one instrument to play.

entries.clue: Spreader of rumours in turn — ruined MP resigns over nothing (12)

indicatorNotes.ruined: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters are wrecked into a new order
indicatorNotes.over: over means on top of, so the nothing is added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A gossip, in turn, reports that a disgraced MP has quit over nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: The nothing joins the MP as fodder before the shuffle; the turn stays in place at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: a person who habitually spreads rumours and tittle-tattle about others.

entries.clue: Person securing home mixed egg with mortar (9)

indicatorNotes.mixed: things mixed are stirred together, like mortar, so the letters are stirred up

annotation.surface: A builder shoring up a house with a bizarre mix of egg and mortar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Securing home' sounds like building work; it means borrowing against a home.
annotation.definitionFit: A financial sense: the borrower pledges a house as security for a loan, so the home secures the debt.

entries.clue: Fairly expensive outing? (5,5)

blocks.note: a meal or night out that costs money

annotation.surface: A night out that costs quite a lot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fairly' reads as 'quite'; it means 'fairly shared', each person paying their own way.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: on this kind of outing each person pays for themselves, so the cost is divided fairly.

entries.clue: So ready and willing to support English (9)

blocks.note: to be for something is to support it

annotation.surface: Someone is eager and keen to back England.
annotation.walkthrough: 'So' is the definition, not an intensifier on 'ready'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words introduce a consequence, meaning for that reason.

entries.clue: Vehicle’s route from terminal reconstructed (8)

indicatorNotes.reconstructed: something reconstructed is rebuilt, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

annotation.surface: A bus route out of a rebuilt terminus.
annotation.walkthrough: The terminal and the route are both transport; only one of them is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the rails set in the street that a tram follows.

entries.clue: Like key parts of Florida or part of New England? Yes and no (7)

annotation.definition: Like key parts of Florida or part of New England? Yes and no

blocks.note: the Keys are a chain of small coral islands

blocks.clueFragment: or part of New England? Yes and no
blocks.note: Rhode Island has the word island in its name but is mostly mainland

annotation.surface: A quiz question about whether Florida's keys or part of New England fit the bill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' is a coral island, so the Florida Keys qualify. Rhode Island, in New England, has 'island' in its name but is mostly mainland, hence 'yes and no'.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the adjective means relating to an island, true of the Keys and only half true of Rhode Island.

entries.clue: Relatively humble person staying out of sight? (7)

blocks.note: the comparative of an adjective meaning modest

annotation.surface: A modest person who keeps out of the spotlight.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented word: split it 3-4 and it names someone who lies low.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: 'relatively' asks for the comparative of lowly, and read in two parts the word is a person lying low.

entries.clue: Top performer runs in behind schedule, badly cut (8)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a verb phrase, cut badly

indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the performer and runs go inside the lateness

blocks.note: an ace is the best at something

annotation.surface: A star player hurries in late and gets a nasty cut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Badly' belongs to the definition, though it tempts as an anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: to tear flesh with a jagged wound, a cut that is a bad one.

entries.clue: Instrument, in France, is put inside that (7)

indicatorNotes.in France: in France means in French, so both small words are translated
indicatorNotes.put inside: put inside means placed within, so the French 'is' goes within the French 'that'

annotation.surface: A musical instrument in France is placed within something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In France' applies to both 'is' and 'that'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the keyboard instrument with bell-like tones heard in Tchaikovsky's Sugar Plum Fairy dance.

entries.clue: Monitoring instrument in audition, one might interfere with play (6)

indicatorNotes.in audition: audition literally means hearing, so the word is taken as heard

annotation.surface: A monitor at a theatre audition who might meddle with the drama.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Audition' and 'play' set a theatre scene; audition also simply means hearing. The Lord Chamberlain censored British plays until 1968.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: an official who cuts or bans material may meddle with a play's script.

entries.clue: Something happening with a beautiful female that’s out of order? (6)

blocks.note: surface padding pointing at the illicit kind

annotation.surface: A liaison with a lovely woman that breaks the rules.
annotation.walkthrough: The tail hints at the illicit kind of affair, one that is out of order, but the definition is the plain sense of an event.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an event or matter, as in 'a grand affair', is something that happens.

entries.clue: Play specific male characters in Romeo and Juliet? (3,3,9,2,6)

annotation.definition: Play specific male characters in Romeo and Juliet?

blocks.note: reads as a verb, to act; means a stage work

blocks.clueFragment: specific male characters in Romeo and Juliet?
blocks.note: the tragedy is set in Verona, so its men come from there

annotation.surface: Casting instructions for the men in Shakespeare's tragedy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Play' reads as a verb about acting; it is the noun. Romeo and Juliet is set in Verona, so its menfolk are gentlemen of Verona.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: Shakespeare's early comedy has a title that could describe men from the setting of his tragedy.

entries.clue: Demand law repealed? (5)

blocks.note: ex = former, no longer in force

annotation.surface: Calling for a law to be struck off.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the opposite order to the clue: the former status first, then the law.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to insist on payment or obedience, as in exacting a price.

entries.clue: Relieve area captured by friendly force (5)

indicatorNotes.captured by: something captured is held prisoner inside, so the area is held within the force

annotation.surface: Troops are relieved when allies seize a region.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relieve' suggests a military relief; it means to ease.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to ease pain, fear or suspicion, as in allaying someone's worries.

entries.clue: Something frowned on in court that whoppers and howlers have in common? (7,8)

annotation.definition2: that whoppers and howlers have in common

blocks.note: a barrister's question that suggests its own answer

blocks.clueFragment: that whoppers and howlers have in common

annotation.surface: Lies and gaffes share a trait that a judge disapproves of.
annotation.walkthrough: Whoppers and howlers both begin with WH, the letters that open question words like who, what and why.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the courtroom term for a question that prompts a witness, and the WH that heads both words, read literally.

entries.clue: Unlike ministers backed after article, extremely unfriendly to others (7)

indicatorNotes.backed: something backed goes backwards, so the word is read in reverse
indicatorNotes.after: after means following, so the reversed word comes behind the others

annotation.surface: Non-clergy supporting a report are highly hostile to other people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' tempts you to take the outer letters of 'unfriendly'; it means SO, and 'unfriendly to others' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: avoiding or disregarding the company of others, without the hostility of antisocial.

entries.clue: Join political moderates in America, first off (5)

indicatorNotes.first off: the first letter is taken off

blocks.note: the US spelling of centre, the moderate middle

annotation.surface: An invitation to sign up with American centrists straight away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First off' looks like 'to begin with'; it deletes the C. 'In America' flags the US spelling.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to become a member of a club or a party in a contest.

entries.clue: Let out — and do so again? (7)

blocks.note: let out a property once more

annotation.surface: Something is set free, and then set free once more.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Let out' is taken twice: to free, and to rent out a property, which done again is RE-LEASE.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: freeing a prisoner, and hyphenated, renting out property a second time.

entries.clue: Enter lair in advance, with serious intent (9)

indicatorNotes.Enter: to enter is to go into something, so the lair goes into the advance

annotation.surface: A burglar gets into the hideout ahead of time, meaning business.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Enter' looks like a verb in the story but is the instruction; 'in advance' is a single piece, not 'in' plus a word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: doing something sincerely and seriously, not in jest.
